request.system:
You are the verifier judge in Ledger. You check whether each clause of an extracted COBOL business rule is supported by the source lines it cites.

For each clause you get its text and the cited lines (marked with >>), with a few surrounding lines for context only. A clause may cite more than one span (for example a statement in the program plus a field declaration in a copybook); judge it on all of its cited spans together. A clause is supported when the cited lines, read with ordinary COBOL semantics, establish what the clause says. Mark it unsupported if it states something the cited lines do not show, gets a condition, comparison, sign, code or message wrong, or relies mainly on lines outside the cited span. Be strict about meaning, not about wording. Give a one-sentence reason either way.

messages.content:
Rule BR-CBTRN02C-005: Route each daily transaction to posting or to the reject file, and set return code 4 when anything is rejected

### given[0] (already verified; context only, no verdict needed): For every daily transaction record read, the processed-transaction count goes up by 1. The failure reason code is reset to 0 and its description to spaces before validation runs.

### given[1] (already verified; context only, no verdict needed): A reject record is 430 bytes. It holds a 350-byte copy of the transaction data followed by an 80-byte validation trailer. The trailer is a 4-digit unsigned reason code followed by a 76-character reason description.

### when[0] (already verified; context only, no verdict needed): After validation, the failure reason code decides what happens: 0 means the transaction is posted, and any other value means it is rejected.

### then[0]: If the reason code is 0, the transaction is posted: the transaction-category balance is updated, then the account record, then the transaction file is written. The reject branch (reject count and reject record) is skipped for that transaction.
fields=['WS-VALIDATION-FAIL-REASON', 'WS-REJECT-COUNT'] literals=['0']
CBTRN02C.cbl:
   207       *              DISPLAY DALYTRAN-RECORD
   208                      MOVE 0 TO WS-VALIDATION-FAIL-REASON
   209                      MOVE SPACES TO WS-VALIDATION-FAIL-REASON-DESC
   210                      PERFORM 1500-VALIDATE-TRAN
>> 211                      IF WS-VALIDATION-FAIL-REASON = 0
>> 212                        PERFORM 2000-POST-TRANSACTION
>> 213                      ELSE
>> 214                        ADD 1 TO WS-REJECT-COUNT
>> 215                        PERFORM 2500-WRITE-REJECT-REC
>> 216                      END-IF
   217                    END-IF
   218                END-IF
   219            END-PERFORM.
   220 
CBTRN02C.cbl:
   436            MOVE  DALYTRAN-ORIG-TS       TO    TRAN-ORIG-TS
   437            PERFORM Z-GET-DB2-FORMAT-TIMESTAMP
   438            MOVE  DB2-FORMAT-TS          TO    TRAN-PROC-TS
   439 
>> 440            PERFORM 2700-UPDATE-TCATBAL
>> 441            PERFORM 2800-UPDATE-ACCOUNT-REC
>> 442            PERFORM 2900-WRITE-TRANSACTION-FILE
   443 
   444            EXIT.
   445 
   446        2500-WRITE-REJECT-REC.

### then[1] (already verified; context only, no verdict needed): If the reason code is not 0, the reject count goes up by 1 and one reject record is written for that transaction.

### then[2] (already verified; context only, no verdict needed): The reject record holds the whole daily transaction record unchanged, followed by the trailer containing the current reason code and description. It is written to the daily rejects file.

### then[3] (already verified; context only, no verdict needed): At the end of the run, the program prints the processed count and the rejected count with fixed labels.

### then[4] (already verified; context only, no verdict needed): If at least one transaction was rejected, the program ends with return code 4. Otherwise the return code is left unchanged.

Give verdicts only for the clauses that are not marked already verified.

content.text: {"verdicts":[{"clause":"then[0]","supported":true,"reason":"Lines 211-216 perform 2000-POST-TRANSACTION when WS-VALIDATION-FAIL-REASON = 0 and put the reject count increment and reject write only in the ELSE branch; lines 440-442, the end of the paragraph just before 2500-WRITE-REJECT-REC, perform 2700-UPDATE-TCATBAL, then 2800-UPDATE-ACCOUNT-REC, then 2900-WRITE-TRANSACTION-FILE in that order."}]}
